title: How GUI Agents Fail: GraceBench for Execution Stability Diagnosis

paragraphs.en: As GUI agents are increasingly deployed for mobile task automation, their reliability depends not only on final task outcomes, but also on whether they reach these outcomes through stable interaction trajectories. In automation workflows, unnecessary actions, detours, and execution errors can add noise to collected data, introduce irreversible side effects, or undermine trust, even when the agent eventually completes the task. It is therefore important to systematically diagnose the execution stability, including whether an agent deviates from a feasible path, enters a loop, becomes stagnant, or recovers from unstable actions. Existing benchmarks, however, primarily assess final task success or a small set of intermediate milestones, leaving step-level execution behavior unclear. To bridge this gap, we introduce GraceBench, an online evaluation framework that represents the reachable interaction space of mobile applications as UI Transition Graphs (UTGs), providing a structural reference for step-level execution diagnosis. To support reliable alignment between dynamic UI observations and graph states, GraceBench uses video-grounded trajectory evaluation over this graph-aligned representation, assessing process stability beyond final success with metrics such as deviation rate, loop burden rate, and recovery ability. GraceBench contains 169 tasks spanning 10 applications and constructs 10 UTGs with 2,909 canonical GUI states and 3,116 observed transitions. Across 3,718 trajectories, GraceBench shows that outcome scores hide execution instability: GPT-5.6 Sol achieves the highest success rate (SR) but the lowest recovery ability, 51.24% of successful runs still contain a deviation or loop, and trajectories with the same success rate (SR) and completion rate (CR) can differ substantially in recovery behavior. Code and data will be released on https://iaie-physicalai.github.io/GraceBench. paragraphs.zh: 随着 GUI 智能体在移动任务自动化中的部署日益广泛，其可靠性不仅取决于最终任务结果，还取决于它们是否通过稳定的交互轨迹达成这些结果。 在自动化工作流程中，不必要的操作、绕路和执行错误可能会为收集的数据引入噪声，造成不可逆的副作用，甚至削弱信任，即便智能体最终完成了任务。 因此，系统性地诊断执行稳定性至关重要，包括判断智能体是否偏离可行路径、陷入循环、停滞不前，或能否从不稳定的操作中恢复。 然而，现有的基准测试主要评估最终任务的成功与否或少数几个中间里程碑，使得步骤级的执行行为仍不明确。 为填补这一空白，我们提出了 GraceBench——一个在线评估框架，它将移动应用程序的可达交互空间表示为 UI 转换图（UTG），从而为步骤级执行诊断提供结构参考。 为了支持动态 UI 观察与图状态之间的可靠对齐，GraceBench 基于该图对齐表示，采用视频辅助的轨迹评估方法，通过偏离率、循环负担率和恢复能力等指标，评估过程稳定性而不仅限于最终成功。 GraceBench 包含覆盖 10 款应用程序的 169 项任务，并构建了 10 个 UTG，其中包含 2,909 个标准 GUI 状态和 3,116 个观察到的转换。 在 3,718 条轨迹中，GraceBench 表明结果分数掩盖了执行的不稳定性：GPT-5.6 Sol 取得了最高的成功率（SR），但恢复能力最低；即使成功运行，仍有 51.24% 包含偏离或循环；而成功率（SR）和完成率（CR）相同的轨迹在恢复行为上可能存在显著差异。 代码和数据将在 https://iaie-physicalai.github.io/GraceBench 上发布。 随着 GUI 智能体在移动任务自动化中的部署日益广泛，其可靠性不仅取决于最终任务结果，还取决于它们是否通过稳定的交互轨迹达成这些结果。 在自动化工作流程中，不必要的操作、绕路和执行错误可能会为收集的数据引入噪声，造成不可逆的副作用，甚至削弱信任，即便智能体最终完成了任务。
